title: Indian-Origin Strategic Expert Ashley Tellis Denies Charges Over Secret Files, Chinese Links | World News - News18
text: Indian-origin strategic expert Ashley Tellis’ lawyers on Wednesday rejected charges that he retained classified documents and met Chinese officials, denying the charges levelled against him. “Ashley J. Tellis is a widely respected scholar and senior policy advisor," his lawyers, Deborah Curtis and John Nassikas, said in a statement. The sexagenarian has held senior positions under former president George W. Bush and remained an unpaid advisor to the US State Department. He faces up to 10 years of prison if the allegations against him are proven. However, his lawyers denied links to China and said that they will ‘vigorously contest’ the charges against him. “We will be vigorously contesting the allegations brought against him, specifically any insinuation of his operating on behalf of a foreign adversary," they said. Meanwhile, top intelligence sources earlier this week while speaking to CNN-News18 said that the arrest of Ashley Tellis in the US shows the depth of Chinese penetration in the Amercian departments The document in question is a secret document on US Air Force techniques and the allegation levelled against Tellis is that he went into the State Department late on September 25 and appeared to print it out. It is alleged that he then met Chinese officials at a restaurant in the Washington suburb of Fairfax, Virginia several time and during one such dinner he appeared to leave a manila envelope. The charges announced by the Justice Department relate to improper handling of documents rather than the meetings, with an FBI special agent saying a search found more than 1,000 pages of top-secret or secret documents in his house. Tellis has been a senior fellow at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, a leading Washington think tank, which said Wednesday that he has been put on administrative leave. Tellis, a naturalized American originally from India, helped negotiate the Bush administration’s civil nuclear cooperation deal with India.
